title: Add bridged on-call context and automated escalation templates
author: Sofia Martinez
ci_status: pass (integration flaky on first run, rerun succeeded)
description: Motivation: on-call responders frequently need full incident context when incidents are bridged across multiple chat channels and paging systems; manual copy/paste is error-prone and slows TTR. This PR introduces a compact, serializable "bridged context" snapshot that travels with the incident across channels and an opinionated library of parameterized escalation templates that the bot can surface or send automatically. Changes include: 1) context capture: snapshot of current runbook pointer, top-3 alerts, recent error rates, and active mitigations; 2) context propagation: add signed metadata token to bridged messages so downstream responders receive identical context; 3) template library: YAML-driven templates with conditional rendering, throttling and dedupe keys; 4) escalation rules: configurable selectors that map alert signals + SLO breach state to template choices and escalation targets; 5) telemetry and auditing: new metrics and audit entries for every template render/send; 6) feature gating: rollout via feature flag per-org with safe defaults. Backwards compatibility: if a downstream bot doesn't understand the token, it ignores it and nothing breaks; templates are opt-in per-oncall rotation. Testing: unit and integration harness simulating bridged Slack<->PagerDuty flows, contract tests for token validity, and an e2e smoke in staging. Rollout: enable for internal SRE rotation (10% of incidents) for 48h, monitor metrics, then expand to all teams. See ENG-4021 for design notes and SUP-912 for support runbook updates. Checklist: [x] design doc linked [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] telemetry added [x] security review requested [x] staged rollout planned.
commits: feat(context): capture bridged channel metadata and ephemeral incident snapshot
feat(templates): add YAML-driven template library and renderer
feat(escalation): implement rule engine for automatic template selection
chore(tests): add simulated slack/pagerduty bridge scenarios
fix(security): sign context tokens with rotated HMAC key and validation
reviews: Ethan Park (requested changes): We should avoid sending full stack traces in context tokens; please confirm we sanitize sensitive fields. Author: sanitized top-level message and excluded traces; also added contract test to assert no secrets are present.

Priya Desai (comment): Template throttling looks good, but what happens when multiple rules match? Author: added deterministic priority ordering and a tiebreaker based on rotation id; documented in templates YAML schema.
Marcus Liu (approved): Verified e2e staging run, metrics look stable and no duplicate escalations observed.
CI Bot: initial integration failed on flaky external-call; author reran pipeline and all checks passed.
Security Review (comment): token signing is acceptable but rotate keys quarterly; author: added key-rotation stub and notes to ops playbook.
release_notes: Adds bridged on-call context propagation and automated escalation templates; feature-gated and opt-in; metrics: bridged_oncall.escalation_sent_total, bridged_oncall.duplicate_dedupe_blocked_total; see docs/runbooks/bridged-context.md for usage.
testing: Unit tests for snapshot and template rendering; integration tests for Slack<->PagerDuty bridging; staging smoke against a snapshot of production data; contract tests to ensure token ABI stability.
rollout_plan: Canary: enable for internal SRE rotation (10% incidents) for 48h -> monitor errors, duplicate escalations, and latency -> 50% teams for 72h -> GA. Feature flag per-org with emergency kill-switch.
risk: low-medium: risk of duplicate escalations if dedupe id generation fails; mitigations: deterministic dedupe keys, rate limits, and audit alerts; security review required before GA.
notes_for_oncall: When enabled, human responders will see a 'bridged context' card with runbook pointer and recent alerts; if auto-escalation triggers, the incident will include the template message and metadata; to opt-out add 'bridged_context: false' to the rotation config.
